question: Vasquez-Morrell Assurance specializes in insuring manufacturers. Whenever a policyholder makes a claim, a claims adjuster determines the amount that Vasquez-Morrell is obligated to pay. Vasquez-Morrell is cutting its staff of claims adjusters by 15 percent. To ensure that the company’s ability to handle claims promptly is affected as little as possible by the staff cuts, consultants recommend that Vasquez-Morrell lay off those adjusters who now take longest, on average, to complete work on claims assigned to them. Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the consultants’ criterion for selecting the staff to be laid off?
option_a: If the time that Vasquez-Morrell takes to settle claims increases significantly, it could lose business to other insurers.
option_b: Supervisors at Vasquez-Morrell tend to assign the most complex claims to the most capable adjusters.
option_c: At Vasquez-Morrell, no insurance payments are made until a claims adjuster has reached a final determination on the claim.
option_d: There are no positions at Vasquez-Morrell to which staff currently employed as claims adjusters could be reassigned.
option_e: The premiums that Vasquez-Morrell currently charges are no higher than those charged for similar coverage by competitors.
explanation: Evaluation of a Plan Situation An insurance company must reduce its staff of claims adjusters. To ensure continuing promptness in handling claims, consultants advise the company to lay off those adjusters who take the longest to complete claims. Reasoning What problem could there be with the criterion? The consultants’ criterion is the time an adjuster takes to settle a claim. However, some claims are naturally more complicated and require more time. If it is true that the company now assigns these time-consuming cases to its most capable adjusters, then these adjusters would be likely to be the ones who take longest to complete their cases. Laying off the adjusters who take the longest would thus mean laying off the company’s most capable staff , which could very well decrease its ability to handle claims promptly. A The consultants’ advice makes sense if increased time to handle claims causes the company to lose business. B Correct. Th is statement properly identifies the problem with the consultants’ criterion. C Th is statement merely describes the process of handling a claim; it does not provide any information about the criterion for layoff s. D The consultants make no recommendations for reassigning staff , so indicating that there are no positions available does not call their advice into question. E The consultants do not recommend a change in premiums; noting that they are similar to competitors’ premiums does not undermine the plan that the consultants recommend.

question: Prolonged spells of hot, dry weather at the end of the grape-growing season typically reduce a vineyard’s yield, because the grapes stay relatively small. In years with such weather, wine producers can make only a relatively small quantity of wine from a given area of vineyards. Nonetheless, in regions where wine producers generally grow their own grapes, analysts typically expect a long, hot, dry spell late in the growing season to result in increased revenues for local wine producers. Which of the following, if true, does most to justify the analysts’ expectation?
option_a: The lower a vineyard’s yield, the less labor is required to harvest the grapes.
option_b: Long, hot, dry spells at the beginning of the grape-growing season are rare, but they can have a devastating effect on a vineyard’s yield.
option_c: Grapes grown for wine production are typically made into wine at or near the vineyard in which they were grown.
option_d: When hot, dry spells are followed by heavy rains, the rains frequently destroy grape crops.
option_e: Grapes that have matured in hot, dry weather make significantly better wine than ordinary grapes.
explanation: Grapes that have matured in hot, dry weather make significantly better wine than ordinary grapes. Argument Construction Situation Hot, dry weather at the end of the grape-growing season reduces yield, so winemakers can only produce a small quantity of wine. However, analysts expect that this weather will increase winemakers’ revenues. Reasoning What additional piece of information explains the analysts’ expectations? The same conditions that lead to low quantity also lead to something that increases revenues. What could this be? If these weather conditions lead to higher-quality wine that will sell for higher prices, the analysts’ expectations for increased revenues are justified. A Lower labor costs mean less expenditure for the winemakers; this does not explain how revenues would increase. B Th is statement about low yields does not explain an increase in revenues. C The proximity of production to the vineyard is irrelevant to the question of how hot, dry weather can be responsible for decreased yield and increased revenues. D Th is statement gives another example of weather’s eff ect on grape crops, but it does not explain how revenues are increased. E Correct. Th is statement properly provides the explanation that the weather conditions will lead to better wines. With better wines typically commanding higher prices, the winemakers will gain the increased revenues that the analysts anticipate.

question: In the past, most children who went sledding in the winter snow in Verland used wooden sleds with runners and steering bars. Ten years ago, smooth plastic sleds became popular; they go faster than wooden sleds but are harder to steer and slow. The concern that plastic sleds are more dangerous is clearly borne out by the fact that the number of children injured while sledding was much higher last winter than it was 10 years ago. Which of the following, if true in Verland, most seriously undermines the force of the evidence cited?
option_a: A few children still use traditional wooden sleds.
option_b: Very few children wear any kind of protective gear, such as helmets, while sledding.
option_c: Plastic sleds can be used in a much wider variety of snow conditions than wooden sleds can.
option_d: Most sledding injuries occur when a sled collides with a tree, a rock, or another sled.
option_e: Because the traditional wooden sleds can carry more than one rider, an accident involving a wooden sled can result in several children being injured.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation Ten years ago, wooden sleds began to be replaced by plastic sleds that go faster but are harder to control. Plastic sleds are more dangerous than wooden sleds because more children suff ered injuries last year than they did 10 years ago. Reasoning What weakens this argument? Th is argument depends on a comparison of two kinds of sleds. Any evidence that would either strengthen or weaken the argument must indicate a comparison. Evidence that applies only to one kind of sled or to both kinds of sleds equally cannot weaken this argument. Consider the implications of the evidence presented in the answer choices. If plastic sleds can be used in a wider variety of conditions than wooden sleds can, then plastic sleds can be used more frequently. It is possible that more frequent use, rather than the sleds themselves, has led to more accidents. A The limited use of some wooden sleds does not weaken the argument. B The absence of protective gear would aff ect accidents with both kinds of sleds. C Correct. Th is statement weakens the argument by providing an alternate explanation for the increased accidents. D Th is statement is true of accidents with both kinds of sleds. E Th is explains why wooden sleds may be dangerous but does not weaken the argument that plastic sleds are even more dangerous.

question: Metal rings recently excavated from seventh-century settlements in the western part of Mexico were made using the same metallurgical techniques as those used by Ecuadorian artisans before and during that period. These techniques are sufficiently complex to make their independent development in both areas unlikely. Since the people of these two areas were in cultural contact, archaeologists hypothesize that the metallurgical techniques used to make the rings found in Mexico were learned by Mexican artisans from Ecuadorian counterparts. Which of the following would it be most useful to establish in order to evaluate the archaeologists’ hypothesis?
option_a: Whether metal objects were traded from Ecuador to western Mexico during the seventh century
option_b: Whether travel between western Mexico and Ecuador in the seventh century would have been primarily by land or by sea
option_c: Whether artisans from western Mexico could have learned complex metallurgical techniques from their Ecuadorian counterparts without actually leaving western Mexico
option_d: Whether metal tools were used in the seventh- century settlements in western Mexico
option_e: Whether any of the techniques used in the manufacture of the metal rings found in western Mexico are still practiced among artisans in Ecuador today
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation Metal rings excavated from seventh-century settlements in western Mexico were made with the same complex techniques used in Ecuador before and during a period when the two cultures were known to be in contact. Mexican artisans are thought to have learned the techniques from Ecuadorian artisans. Reasoning What point could best be applied in evaluating this hypothesis? Consider what specific information would help to assess the archaeologists’ theory. It is given that the two areas had some cultural contact. If it were determined that metal objects were traded from one culture to the other, it could be possible that the metalworking techniques were passed along as well. Such evidence would be relevant to the hypothesis that Mexican artisans saw the work of their Ecuadorian counterparts and, from this exchange, learned the techniques to make the metal rings. A Correct. Th is statement properly identifies information that would be useful in the evaluation of the archaeologists’ hypothesis. B The means of travel is irrelevant to the hypothesis about the source of the techniques. C The hypothesis is not about where Mexican artisans learned the techniques, but whether they learned them from the Ecuadorians. D The existence of metal tools provides no helpful information in establishing whether the Ecuadorians were the source of the metallurgical techniques. E The comparison to the present day is irrelevant to the hypothesis.

question: Following several years of declining advertising sales, the Greenville Times reorganized its advertising sales force. Before reorganization, the sales force was organized geographically, with some sales representatives concentrating on city-center businesses and others concentrating on different outlying regions. The reorganization attempted to increase the sales representatives’ knowledge of clients’ businesses by having each sales representative deal with only one type of industry or of retailing. After the reorganization, revenue from advertising sales increased. In assessing whether the improvement in advertising sales can properly be attributed to the reorganization, it would be most helpful to find out which of the following?
option_a: What proportion of the total revenue of the Greenville Times is generated by advertising sales?
option_b: Has the circulation of the Greenville Times increased substantially in the last two years?
option_c: Among all the types of industry and retailing that use the Greenville Times as an advertising vehicle, which type accounts for the largest proportion of the newspaper’s advertising sales?
option_d: Do any clients of the sales representatives of the Greenville Times have a standing order with the Times for a fixed amount of advertising per month?
option_e: Among the advertisers in the Greenville Times, are there more types of retail business or more types of industrial business?
explanation: Evaluation of a Plan Situation In the face of declining advertising sales, a newspaper reorganizes its sales force so that sales representatives have a better understanding of businesses. Revenue from advertising sales increased after the reorganization. Reasoning What additional evidence would help determine the source of the increased revenue? In order to attribute the increased revenue to the reorganization of the sales force, other possible causes must be eliminated. Newspaper advertising rates are linked to circulation; when circulation increases, higher rates can be charged and revenues will increase. An alternate explanation might be a significant rise in circulation, so it would be particularly helpful to know if circulation had increased. A The question concerns only increased revenue from advertising sales; the proportion of advertising revenue to total revenue is outside the scope of the question. B Correct. Th is statement provides another possible explanation for increased revenue of advertising sales, and so the answer to this question would help to clarify the reason for the increased revenue. C Knowing how the advertising sales break down by type of business might be useful for other purposes, but it does not help to show the cause of the increase. D A fixed amount of advertising would not explain increased revenue, so the answer to this question would be irrelevant. E Distinguishing between the types of businesses will not contribute to determining whether the reorganization was responsible for the increased revenue.

question: Motorists in a certain country frequently complain that traffic congestion is much worse now than it was 20 years ago. No real measure of how much traffic congestion there was 20 years ago exists, but the motorists’ complaints are almost certainly unwarranted. The country’s highway capacity has tripled in the last twenty years, thanks to a vigorous highway construction program, whereas the number of automobiles registered in the country has increased by only 75 percent. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
option_a: Most automobile travel is local, and the networks of roads and streets in the country’s settled areas have changed little over the last 20 years.
option_b: Gasoline prices are high, and miles traveled per car per year have not changed much over the last 20 years.
option_c: The country’s urban centers have well-developed public transit systems that carry most of the people who commute into those centers.
option_d: The average age of automobiles registered in the country is lower now than it was 20 years ago.
option_e: Radio stations have long been broadcasting regular traffic reports that inform motorists about traffic congestion.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation Motorists complain that traffic congestion in their country is much worse than it was twenty years ago. But these complaints have no basis since the highway capacity in this country has tripled in the same period, whereas the number of cars registered has risen by only 75 percent. Reasoning Which point most undermines the argument that the complaints are unwarranted? Consider that the response to the generalized complaints about congestion discusses only the topic of highway capacity. What if the congestion that motorists are complaining about is not on highways but on local roads? Discovering that travel tends to be local in this country and that the local roads have not been improved in the last twenty years would seriously weaken the argument. A Correct. Th is statement properly identifies a weakness in the argument: the response to the broad complaint addresses a diff erent subject, highway capacity, not the issue of traffic congestion encountered by most motorists. B If high gas prices actually prevented motorists from driving, and if motorists’ driving habits were the same as they were twenty years ago, then these points should strengthen the argument that there is no basis for their complaints. C The number of commuters who use public transit does not aff ect the argument that the motorists’ complaints have no basis. D The age of registered cars is irrelevant to the argument. E The radio broadcasts attest to the existence of traffic, but not to its increase, so they do not aff ect the argument.

question: The percentage of households with an annual income of more than $40,000 is higher in Merton County than in any other county. However, the percentage of households with an annual income of $60,000 or more is higher in Sommer County. If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true?
option_a: The percentage of households with an annual income of $80,000 is higher in Sommer County than in Merton County.
option_b: Merton County has the second highest percentage of households with an annual income of $60,000 or more.
option_c: Some households in Merton County have an annual income between $40,000 and $60,000.
option_d: The number of households with an annual income of more than $40,000 is greater in Merton County than in Sommer County.
option_e: Average annual household income is higher in Sommer County than in Merton County.
explanation: Merton has the highest share of households above $40,000, so its share is at least as high as Sommer’s. Sommer’s share at $60,000 or more is higher than Merton’s. So Merton’s share above $40,000 must be larger than its own share at $60,000 or more, which means some Merton households earn between $40,000 and $60,000. The statement about $80,000 incomes can’t be determined from the given percentages. The claim that Merton is second highest at $60,000 or more can’t be determined either. The claim about the number of households can’t be drawn from percentages. The claim about average income can’t be determined from the information given.

question: Tiger beetles are such fast runners that they can capture virtually any nonflying insect. However, when running toward an insect, a tiger beetle will intermittently stop and then, a moment later, resume its attack. Perhaps the beetles cannot maintain their pace and must pause for a moment’s rest; but an alternative hypothesis is that while running, tiger beetles are unable to adequately process the resulting rapidly changing visual information and so quickly go blind and stop. Which of the following, if discovered in experiments using artificially moved prey insects, would support one of the two hypotheses and undermine the other?
option_a: When a prey insect is moved directly toward a beetle that has been chasing it, the beetle immediately stops and runs away without its usual intermittent stopping.
option_b: In pursuing a swerving insect, a beetle alters its course while running and its pauses become more frequent as the chase progresses.
option_c: In pursuing a moving insect, a beetle usually responds immediately to changes in the insect’s direction, and it pauses equally frequently whether the chase is up or down an incline.
option_d: If, when a beetle pauses, it has not gained on the insect it is pursuing, the beetle generally ends its pursuit.
option_e: The faster a beetle pursues an insect fleeing directly away from it, the more frequently the beetle stops.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation Two hypotheses are off ered to explain the sudden stop that tiger beetles make while pursuing their prey: (1) they cannot maintain the rapid pace and must rest, and (2) they run too quickly to process visual information and so temporarily go blind. Reasoning What point would strengthen one of the two hypotheses and weaken the other? Consider the information provided in each answer choice, remembering that information that supports one hypothesis must necessarily detract from the other. Any information that is not about pursuit or that aff ects the two hypotheses equally may be dismissed from consideration. If the frequency of stopping increases when the beetle follows a swerving insect and must constantly change its course, then the second hypothesis is strengthened; the beetle’s pauses increase as the variety of visual information that it needs to deal with increases. A The hypotheses concern ongoing pursuit; since this information is not about the beetle’s continuing pursuit of prey, it neither strengthens nor weakens either hypothesis. B Correct. Th is statement provides information that strengthens the second hypothesis: the swerving pursuit and the resulting continual course adjustments appear to be forcing the beetle to stop with increasing frequency to sort out the erratic visual information. C In this experiment, since neither vision nor tiredness appears to be problematic, the beetle could be stopping for either reason; this information neither strengthens nor weakens either hypothesis. D Th is information is irrelevant since both the hypotheses are about mid-pursuit behaviors. E The correlation of frequency of stops with speed aff ects both hypotheses equally; the pauses could be equally due to an inability to maintain the pace or due to a need to process the visual information.

question: Guillemots are birds of Arctic regions. They feed on fish that gather beneath thin sheets of floating ice, and they nest on nearby land. Guillemots need 80 consecutive snow-free days in a year to raise their chicks, so until average temperatures in the Arctic began to rise recently, the guillemots’ range was limited to the southernmost Arctic coast. Therefore, if the warming continues, the guillemots’ range will probably be enlarged by being extended northward along the coast. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
option_a: Even if the warming trend continues, there will still be years in which guillemot chicks are killed by an unusually early snow.
option_b: If the Arctic warming continues, guillemots’ current predators are likely to succeed in extending their own range farther north.
option_c: Guillemots nest in coastal areas, where temperatures are generally higher than in inland areas.
option_d: If the Arctic warming continues, much of the thin ice in the southern Arctic will disappear.
option_e: The fish that guillemots eat are currently preyed on by a wider variety of predators in the southernmost Arctic regions than they are farther north.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation In the southern Arctic, guillemots find their prey beneath thin sheets of ice, nest nearby, and require 80 snow-free days to raise their young. A warming trend means that their range may be enlarged by extending northward along the coast. Reasoning Which point weakens the argument about the enlargement of the guillemots’ range? How could the birds move northward and simultaneously not enlarge their range? Consider the assumption implied by the idea of enlargement. If the guillemots lost their southern habitat, then their northward move would be a displacement rather than an enlargement. If their source of food was no longer available to them in the southern Arctic, then they would abandon that area as part of their range. A An exceptional year is not an argument against an enlarged range because an unusually early snow could happen in the southern Arctic as well. B If their current predators also migrate northward, then the guillemots’ situation has not changed, so this is not an argument against their enlarged range. C The argument suggests that they will move not inland, but northward along the coast. D Correct. Th is statement properly identifies a factor that weakens the argument: the guillemots’ move northward would not enlarge their range if they lost their food source, fish found under thin ice, in the southern Arctic. E The possibility that they may find prey more easily in the north does not mean that they would abandon the southern Arctic, and so this point does not weaken the argument.

question: Some batches of polio vaccine used around 1960 were contaminated with SV40, a virus that in monkeys causes various cancers. Some researchers now claim that this contamination caused some cases of a certain cancer in humans, mesothelioma. This claim is not undercut by the fact that a very careful survey made in the 1960s of people who had received the contaminated vaccine found no elevated incidence of any cancer, since ____________.
option_a: most cases of mesothelioma are caused by exposure to asbestos
option_b: in some countries, there was no contamination of the vaccine
option_c: SV40 is widely used in laboratories to produce cancers in animals
option_d: mesotheliomas take several decades to develop
option_e: mesothelioma was somewhat less common in 1960 than it is now
explanation: The survey in the 1960s found no increase in cancer, yet researchers still claim the vaccine caused some mesothelioma. That is consistent only if the cancer takes decades to develop, because the survey was done too soon after exposure to show any cases. The statement about asbestos does not explain why the survey missed the effect. The statement about countries with no contamination is irrelevant to the survey. The statement about SV40 being used in laboratories adds nothing about the survey’s timing. The statement that mesothelioma was less common in 1960 does not explain why the survey found no increase.

question: Gortland has long been narrowly self-sufficient in both grain and meat. However, as per capita income in Gortland has risen toward the world average, per capita consumption of meat has also risen toward the world average, and it takes several pounds of grain to produce one pound of meat. Therefore, since per capita income continues to rise, whereas domestic grain production will not increase, Gortland will soon have to import either grain or meat or both. Which of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?
option_a: The total acreage devoted to grain production in Gortland will soon decrease.
option_b: Importing either grain or meat will not result in a significantly higher percentage of Gortlanders’ incomes being spent on food than is currently the case.
option_c: The per capita consumption of meat in Gortland is increasing at roughly the same rate across all income levels.
option_d: The per capita income of meat producers in Gortland is rising faster than the per capita income of grain producers.
option_e: People in Gortland who increase their consumption of meat will not radically decrease their consumption of grain.
explanation: People in Gortland who increase their consumption of meat will not radically decrease their consumption of grain. Argument Construction Situation A country previously self-sufficient in grain and meat will soon have to import one or the other or both. Consumption of meat has risen as per capita income has risen, and it takes several pounds of grain to produce one pound of meat. Reasoning What conditions must be true for the conclusion to be true? Meat consumption is rising. What about grain consumption? A sharp reduction in the amount of grain consumed could compensate for increased meat consumption, making the conclusion false. If people did radically decrease their grain consumption, it might not be necessary to import grain or meat or both. Since the argument concludes that the imports are necessary, it assumes grain consumption will not plunge. A The argument makes no assumptions about the acreage devoted to grain; it assumes only that the demand for grain will rise. B The argument does not discuss the percentage of their income that Gortlanders spend on food, so an assumption about this topic is not needed. C The argument involves only meat consumption in general, not its distribution by income level. D Since the argument does not refer to the incomes of meat producers and grain producers, it cannot depend on an assumption about them. E Correct. Th is statement properly identifies the assumption that there will be no great decrease in grain consumption.

question: The Hazelton coal-processing plant is a major employer in the Hazelton area, but national environmental regulations will force it to close if it continues to use old, polluting processing methods. However, to update the plant to use newer, cleaner methods would be so expensive that the plant will close unless it receives the tax break it has requested. In order to prevent a major increase in local unemployment, the Hazelton government is considering granting the plant’s request. Which of the following would be most important for the Hazelton government to determine before deciding whether to grant the plant’s request?
option_a: Whether the company that owns the plant would open a new plant in another area if the present plant were closed
option_b: Whether the plant would employ far fewer workers when updated than it does now
option_c: Whether the level of pollutants presently being emitted by the plant is high enough to constitute a health hazard for local residents
option_d: Whether the majority of the coal processed by the plant is sold outside the Hazelton area
option_e: Whether the plant would be able to process more coal when updated than it does now
explanation: Evaluation of a Plan Situation Because of the expenses of mandatory updating, a plant that is a major employer in the local area will close unless it receives the tax break it has requested from the local government. Reasoning What point is most critical to the evaluation of the request? Consider the information provided in the answer choices. The plant is important to the local government primarily because it is a major employer of local residents. What if updating the plant significantly reduced the number of employees needed? It is crucial for the local government to determine whether the plant will continue to employ the same number of people once it has updated. A The local government is concerned only with the local area, so a new site outside that area is irrelevant. B Correct. Th is statement properly identifies a factor that is critical to the plant’s argument and the local government’s decision. C Updating is mandatory under national environmental regulations, whether the local residents are aff ected by the plant’s pollutants or not. D At issue is the plant’s role as a major employer; where its product is sold is irrelevant. E The amount of coal processed by the updated plant is irrelevant to the critical issue of the number of people employed to process that coal.

question: A physically active lifestyle has been shown to help increase longevity. In the Wistar region of Bellaria, the average age at death is considerably higher than in any other part of the country. Wistar is the only mountainous part of Bellaria. A mountainous terrain makes even such basic activities as walking relatively strenuous; it essentially imposes a physically active lifestyle on people. Clearly, this circumstance explains the long lives of people in Wistar. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
option_a: In Bellaria all medical expenses are paid by the government, so that personal income does not affect the quality of health care a person receives.
option_b: The Wistar region is one of Bellaria’s least populated regions.
option_c: Many people who live in the Wistar region have moved there in middle age or upon retirement.
option_d: The many opportunities for hiking, skiing, and other outdoor activities that Wistar’s mountains offer make it a favorite destination for vacationing Bellarians.
option_e: Per capita spending on recreational activities is no higher in Wistar than it is in other regions of Bellaria.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation People in one region of a country live longer than people in other areas. The higher average age at time of death is attributed to the healthy lifestyle of the people in this region, where the mountainous terrain demands a physically active life. Reasoning What point weakens the argument? Consider what assumption underlies the argument that the physically active lifestyle required of living in Wistar is responsible for its residents’ relative longevity. The mountainous environment necessitates lifelong levels of rigorous physical activity that build a more robust population. What if a significant portion of the population has not been conditioned since childhood to the demands of the terrain? It is assumed here that the healthy lifestyle imposed by the terrain has shaped residents from birth and accounts for their longer life span. If many residents only moved there later in life, the argument is weakened. A The argument is not about the quality of health care throughout the country, but the length of the residents’ lives in a particular region. B The rate of population density does not aff ect the argument. C Correct. Th is statement properly identifies a point that weakens the argument. D The area’s popularity as a vacation destination does not aff ect the longevity of the local residents. E The argument establishes that merely living in the region is strenuous; the spending on recreational activities is irrelevant.

question: Cheever College offers several online courses via remote computer connection, in addition to traditional classroom-based courses. A study of student performance at Cheever found that, overall, the average student grade for online courses matched that for classroom-based courses. In this calculation of the average grade, course withdrawals were weighted as equivalent to a course failure, and the rate of withdrawal was much lower for students enrolled in classroom-based courses than for students enrolled in online courses. If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true of Cheever College?
option_a: Among students who did not withdraw, students enrolled in online courses got higher grades, on average, than students enrolled in classroom- based courses.
option_b: The number of students enrolled per course at the start of the school term is much higher, on average, for the online courses than for the classroom-based courses.
option_c: There are no students who take both an online and a classroom-based course in the same school term.
option_d: Among Cheever College students with the best grades, a significant majority take online, rather than classroom-based, courses.
option_e: Courses offered online tend to deal with subject matter that is less challenging than that of classroom-based courses.
explanation: Withdrawals count as failures, and online courses have a much higher withdrawal rate. Even so, average grades match those of classroom courses. For that to happen, the online students who stayed must have earned higher grades on average to make up for the withdrawals. The statement about enrollment per course cannot be worked out from grade averages. The statement about students taking both kinds of course is not supported. The statement about the best students cannot be drawn from averages. The statement about subject difficulty has no support in the information given.

question: For years the beautiful Renaissance buildings in Palitito have been damaged by exhaust from the many tour buses that come to the city. There has been little parking space, so most buses have idled at the curb during each stop on their tour, and idling produces as much exhaust as driving. The city has now provided parking that accommodates a third of the tour buses, so damage to Palitito’s buildings from the buses’ exhaust will diminish significantly. Which of the following, if true, most strongly supports the argument?
option_a: The exhaust from Palitito’s few automobiles is not a significant threat to Palitito’s buildings.
option_b: Palitito’s Renaissance buildings are not threatened by pollution other than engine exhaust.
option_c: Tour buses typically spend less than one-quarter of the time they are in Palitito transporting passengers from one site to another.
option_d: More tourists come to Palitito by tour bus than by any other single means of transportation.
option_e: Some of the tour buses that are unable to find parking drive around Palitito while their passengers are visiting a site.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation Tour buses have damaged Renaissance buildings with their exhaust fumes because lack of parking has kept the buses idling at curbs. Providing new parking for a third of the buses should significantly reduce the damage caused by the exhaust. Reasoning What point strengthens the argument? The argument for reduced damage relies on the reduction of the vehicles’ exhaust fumes. Any additional evidence regarding the extent to which the vehicular emissions are likely to be reduced also supports the argument for the benefits of the new parking spaces. Learning that tour buses spend not just a few minutes but most of their time idling at the curb strengthens the argument. The new parking spaces will allow a third of the tour buses to spend 75 percent of their time with their engines off , causing no damage at all. A If automobile exhaust is not a threat, the argument is not aff ected. B Th is statement does not address the question of whether the new parking will reduce the damage caused by engine exhaust from the buses. C Correct. Th is statement properly cites a factor that supports the argument: since most of the buses’ time has been spent producing damaging exhaust, the new parking should reduce the damage significantly. D Th is statement about tourists’ chosen means of transportation is irrelevant to the issue of what the buses do while in the city. E It is given that the new parking will only provide space for a third of the buses, and thus some buses will continue to idle and some to drive around, continuing to contribute equally to the building damage. Th is statement does not strengthen the argument.

question: During the 1980s and 1990s, the annual number of people who visited the Sordellian Mountains increased continually, and many new ski resorts were built. Over the same period, however, the number of visitors to ski resorts who were caught in avalanches decreased, even though there was no reduction in the annual number of avalanches in the Sordellian Mountains. Which of the following, if true in the Sordellian Mountains during the 1980s and 1990s, most helps to explain the decrease?
option_a: Avalanches were most likely to happen when a large new snowfall covered an older layer of snow.
option_b: Avalanches destroyed at least some buildings in the Sordellian Mountains in every year.
option_c: People planning new ski slopes and other resort facilities used increasingly accurate information about which locations are likely to be in the path of avalanches.
option_d: The average length of stay for people visiting the Sordellian Mountains increased slightly.
option_e: Construction of new ski resorts often led to the clearing of wooded areas that had helped to prevent avalanches.
explanation: More visitors came and the number of avalanches stayed the same, yet fewer visitors were caught in avalanches. If planners used increasingly accurate information about where avalanches are likely to travel, they could build new slopes and facilities away from those paths, so fewer visitors would be exposed. The statement about when avalanches are most likely to happen is unchanged over time, so it explains nothing. The statement about buildings destroyed does not explain the drop in visitors caught. The statement about longer stays points to more exposure, not less. The statement about cleared woodland would make avalanches more dangerous, which is the opposite of what needs explaining.

question: A year ago, Dietz Foods launched a yearlong advertising campaign for its canned tuna. Last year Dietz sold 12 million cans of tuna compared to the 10 million sold during the previous year, an increase directly attributable to new customers brought in by the campaign. Profits from the additional sales, however, were substantially less than the cost of the advertising campaign. Clearly, therefore, the campaign did nothing to further Dietz’s economic interests. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?
option_a: Sales of canned tuna account for a relatively small percentage of Dietz Foods’ profits.
option_b: Most of the people who bought Dietz’s canned tuna for the first time as a result of the campaign were already loyal customers of other Dietz products.
option_c: A less expensive advertising campaign would have brought in significantly fewer new customers for Dietz’s canned tuna than did the campaign Dietz Foods launched last year.
option_d: Dietz made money on sales of canned tuna last year.
option_e: In each of the past five years, there was a steep, industry-wide decline in sales of canned tuna.
explanation: Argument Evaluation Situation An advertising campaign was responsible for increased sales of canned tuna. Since the profits from the increased sales were less than the costs of the campaign, the campaign did not contribute to the company’s economic interests. Reasoning Which point weakens the argument? Consider the basis of the argument: if profits are lower than costs, the campaign made no contribution to the company’s financial well-being. In what case might this be untrue? What if the advertising campaign reversed an industry-wide trend of declining sales? If Dietz experienced increasing sales, while other companies experienced decreased sales, then the campaign did contribute to the economic interests of the company, and the argument is considerably weakened. A The issue is not the percentage of profits that canned tuna contributes, but the success of the advertising campaign. B If the customers bought the tuna because of the campaign, it is irrelevant to the argument that they also bought other Dietz products. C Th is information neither strengthens nor weakens the argument. D The argument is not about profits only, but about whether the advertising campaign contributed to the economic interests of the company. E Correct. Th is statement properly identifies a factor that weakens the argument: the campaign secured the benefits of increased sales at a time when the entire industry was experiencing a decline in sales.

question: Veloce, a manufacturer of high-end running shoes, sells its footwear exclusively through independent specialty running stores, where staff provide personalized fittings and recommendations to customers. To increase its profits, Veloce plans to begin selling its shoes directly to consumers through its own website at prices lower than the retail prices charged by the specialty stores. Veloce's management reasons that eliminating the wholesale discount offered to retailers will increase the company's profit margin on each pair sold, thereby increasing overall company profits. Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the likelihood that Veloce's plan will succeed?
option_a: Independent specialty running stores typically earn a larger share of their overall revenue from athletic apparel than from running shoes.
option_b: Many runners who buy shoes online regularly order multiple pairs in different sizes with the intention of returning those that do not fit.
option_c: Specialty running stores are likely to stop stocking and recommending Veloce shoes if the manufacturer undercuts their retail prices online.
option_d: Consumers who purchase high-end running shoes are generally less sensitive to price differences than are consumers of entry-level athletic footwear.
option_e: Veloce's manufacturing capacity is currently sufficient to produce enough shoes to meet a moderate increase in total demand.
explanation: Veloce's plan assumes that higher margins on direct-to-consumer sales will boost overall profits. However, the premise notes that sales currently depend on specialty store staff providing personalized fittings and recommendations. If those stores drop Veloce products because Veloce is undercutting them online, the company could lose its primary driver of customer acquisition and the bulk of its sales volume, causing overall profits to decline despite higher per-pair margins.

question: In an effort to reduce passenger delays, the city of Belton replaced all turnstiles at its busiest commuter rail stations with high-speed automated fare gates. The new gates reduced the average time passengers spent passing through the station entrances by over seventy percent. However, during the six months following the installation, the average total commute time for passengers traveling through these stations during peak morning hours actually increased, even though train schedules and total passenger volume remained unchanged. Which of the following, if true, most helps to explain the paradoxical result described above?
option_a: The ongoing maintenance costs for the automated fare gates were significantly higher than the city had originally budgeted.
option_b: By clearing entry points more quickly, passengers converged onto platforms in denser groups, causing prolonged boarding delays that repeatedly caused trains to depart late.
option_c: Many passengers who previously used paper tickets switched to reloadable transit cards after the new gates were installed.
option_d: The automated fare gates reduced fare evasion, leading to a substantial increase in ticket revenue for the rail network.
option_e: The commuter rail system operates with the same number of passenger cars per train during peak morning hours as it does during off-peak hours.
explanation: Choice B provides an explanation for how speeding up entry into the station could paradoxically increase total commute time: by funneling commuters onto platforms in sudden, dense clusters rather than a steady trickle, train boarding became more congested and took longer, resulting in cascading train departure delays that lengthened overall commutes.

question: To reduce automotive air pollution, the municipal government of Ardenville recently offered a voucher program that reimburses residents for 25 percent of the purchase price of an electric bicycle. City planners project that thousands of residents will participate and that each participant will ride their electric bicycle for several hundred miles per year. On the basis of these projections, the planners conclude that the program will lead to a substantial decrease in automobile emissions in Ardenville over the next two years. Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the planners' conclusion?
option_a: A large majority of the residents who plan to use the vouchers currently commute by walking, using conventional bicycles, or riding public transit.
option_b: The regional power grid that will charge the electric bicycles produces a fraction of the emissions per mile that a typical gasoline passenger car produces.
option_c: The voucher program does not cover the routine maintenance costs associated with keeping an electric bicycle operational.
option_d: Automobile traffic congestion in Ardenville is generally worse during the winter months, when bicycle usage typically declines.
option_e: The total municipal funding allocated to the voucher program is less than what Ardenville spends annually on roadway repaving.
explanation: The planners' conclusion depends on the assumption that miles ridden on the newly purchased electric bicycles will displace miles that would otherwise have been driven in automobiles. If, as option A states, the majority of voucher recipients are replacing walking, conventional cycling, or public transit rather than car trips, the increase in electric bicycle mileage will not correspond to a substantial drop in automobile use or emissions, thereby undermining the conclusion.

question: Two years ago, the municipality of Oakridge installed automated red-light cameras at ten of its busiest intersections to decrease the number of traffic accidents caused by drivers running red lights. In the two years since the installation, the number of rear-end collisions at these intersections increased by 30 percent, while the total number of vehicular accidents at the intersections remained unchanged. Based on these data, a local safety group concluded that the installation of the red-light cameras failed to improve motorist safety at those intersections. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the safety group's conclusion?
option_a: Motorists who receive citations issued by the automated cameras rarely contest the fines in municipal court.
option_b: Most motorists in Oakridge were aware of the locations of the red-light cameras within weeks of their installation.
option_c: Neighboring municipalities that installed similar red-light cameras also recorded an increase in rear-end collisions.
option_d: Side-impact collisions, which typically result in far more severe injuries and fatalities than rear-end collisions, decreased substantially at the monitored intersections.
option_e: The fine revenue generated by the automated cameras exceeded the municipality's cost of maintaining the equipment.
explanation: The safety group equates the overall number of accidents directly with motorist safety. If side-impact collisions (which cause far more severe injuries and fatalities) decreased substantially and were merely replaced in number by minor rear-end collisions, then the overall severity of accidents fell, meaning motorist safety did in fact improve despite the total number of accidents remaining the same.

question: In the nation of Marland, the opening of a high-speed rail line between its two largest cities led to a 30 percent decline in the number of passengers flying between them. Transport planners in neighboring Sylvanica plan to build a high-speed rail line between Sylvanica's two primary cities, Port Vance and Eldergate, which are separated by a distance comparable to that between the two Marland cities. The planners project that the new line will produce a similar decline in air travel between Port Vance and Eldergate. Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the transport planners' projection?
option_a: The projected ticket price for a high-speed train trip between Port Vance and Eldergate is substantially lower than current airfares for that route.
option_b: A significant proportion of residents in both Port Vance and Eldergate own private automobiles and frequently use them for intercity travel.
option_c: The construction costs per mile for high-speed rail infrastructure in Sylvanica are significantly higher than those incurred in Marland.
option_d: High-speed rail service between Port Vance and Eldergate will take roughly the same amount of time as the total travel time required when flying.
option_e: The vast majority of passengers who fly between Port Vance and Eldergate are travelers transferring to or from international flights at Port Vance's airport.
explanation: The planners' projection assumes that travelers currently flying between Port Vance and Eldergate can and will switch to high-speed rail. However, if the vast majority of these fliers are connecting passengers transferring to or from international flights at the airport, they are far less likely to substitute rail for air travel, as doing so would require separate ticketing, luggage re-checking, and transit to the airport.

question: Agronomists have developed a new variety of wheat, dubbed Cerena, that produces higher grain yields while requiring 25 percent less water per acre than standard wheat varieties. In field trials under normal growing conditions, Cerena plots required significantly less water and produced 15 percent more grain per acre than adjacent plots planted with standard wheat. Consequently, the researchers concluded that if farmers in arid regions replace standard wheat with Cerena, the total amount of water consumed by agriculture in those regions will decline significantly. Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the researchers' conclusion?
option_a: The nutritional profile of grain produced by Cerena is virtually indistinguishable from that of grain produced by standard wheat varieties.
option_b: In the arid regions, the total acreage that farmers dedicate to crop cultivation is limited primarily by the volume of water available for irrigation.
option_c: Cerena requires the application of fertilizers that are slightly more expensive than those typically used with standard wheat.
option_d: Standard wheat varieties can be stored for longer periods after harvest than Cerena without spoilage.
option_e: Rainfall in arid regions is subject to greater year-to-year variation than rainfall in the regions where the field trials were conducted.
explanation: The researchers assume that using a crop that requires less water per acre will result in a decrease in total agricultural water consumption. However, if the total acreage that farmers can cultivate is constrained primarily by the supply of water available for irrigation (as stated in option B), farmers who switch to Cerena will likely use the water saved per acre to bring additional, previously uncultivated land into production. Consequently, they will continue to consume all or most of the available water, preventing a significant decline in total agricultural water consumption.

question: To reduce traffic congestion during peak morning hours, the city of Varna constructed a commuter rail line connecting its outer suburbs directly to the central business district. A year after the rail service began, daily ridership reached the transit authority's target of 25,000 passenger trips each morning. Nevertheless, traffic monitoring sensors indicated that the volume of automobile traffic on the major highways leading into the city during the morning rush hour did not decline at all. Which of the following would be most useful to determine in explaining why the opening of the rail line failed to reduce highway traffic volume?
option_a: Whether the majority of the rail line's morning passengers had previously traveled to the business district by private automobile rather than by other transit modes
option_b: Whether the average travel time for commuters taking the train was significantly less than the travel time for those driving on the highway
option_c: Whether retail businesses located near suburban train stations experienced an increase in sales after the rail service began
option_d: Whether the transit authority offered subsidized monthly passes to employees of large corporations located in the business district
option_e: Whether the municipal government intends to extend the commuter rail network to additional outlying communities
explanation: If the majority of the rail line's riders were people who previously took other forms of public transit (such as express buses) rather than driving their own cars, the train would not have removed a significant number of automobiles from the highways, which directly explains the lack of decline in highway congestion. Conversely, if they were previously private automobile drivers, the explanation must lie elsewhere (e.g., latent demand or overall population growth).

question: Archaeologists excavating a twelfth-century BCE coastal settlement in the Levant uncovered numerous bronze tools. Laboratory analysis revealed that the copper in these tools matches the unique isotopic signature of ore mined exclusively on the island of Cyprus. Because tin, the other essential component of bronze, was entirely absent from the Mediterranean basin and had to be imported from Central Asia, historians have concluded that the settlement's metal artisans maintained trade relationships with suppliers from both Cyprus and Central Asia. Which of the following is an assumption on which the historians' conclusion depends?
option_a: The settlement's merchants did not trade directly with regions located farther east than Central Asia.
option_b: The bronze tools discovered at the settlement were cast locally rather than imported as finished goods.
option_c: Copper from Cyprus was the only type of metal used by artisans in the Levant during the twelfth century BCE.
option_d: The quantity of tin required to produce bronze tools was roughly equal to the quantity of copper required.
option_e: Maritime trade routes between Cyprus and the Levant were significantly safer than overland trade routes from Central Asia.
explanation: The historians conclude that the settlement's artisans had trade connections with both regions because the bronze tools found at the site contain Cypriot copper and Central Asian tin. For this evidence to support the conclusion about the local artisans, the tools must have actually been crafted by those artisans from raw materials. If the tools had been imported as finished products from elsewhere, the local artisans would not need to have had any trade connections with copper or tin suppliers. Therefore, option B is an essential assumption. Option A is incorrect because trading with regions further east would not prevent the artisans from trading with Central Asia. Option C is too extreme and irrelevant; the argument only requires that this specific copper came from Cyprus, not that no other metals were used. Option D is irrelevant because the physical proportions of tin and copper do not affect whether trade relationships were maintained. Option E is irrelevant because the relative safety of the transport routes does not affect whether the trade connections existed.

question: In professional baseball, pitchers face a high risk of tearing the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in their throwing elbow, an injury caused by mechanical stress during high-velocity pitches. A sports technology company recently created a wearable sleeve that measures the rotational torque on a pitcher's elbow during every throw. The company claims that baseball teams can dramatically reduce the incidence of UCL tears by having pitchers wear the sleeve during games and removing any pitcher from the mound as soon as the sleeve detects that the torque on his elbow has exceeded a designated safety threshold. Which of the following would be most useful to determine in evaluating the company's claim?
option_a: Whether pitchers are significantly more likely to experience UCL tears during cold-weather games than during warm-weather games
option_b: Whether wearing the sleeve causes minor physical discomfort that impairs a pitcher's command and accuracy
option_c: Whether pitchers who suffer UCL tears typically exhibit elevated elbow torque across multiple pitches before a tear occurs
option_d: Whether relief pitchers experience higher average elbow torque per pitch than starting pitchers do
option_e: Whether surgical repair of a torn UCL is more successful now than it was in previous decades
explanation: The company claims that pulling a pitcher once elbow torque exceeds a safety threshold will dramatically reduce UCL tears. For this strategy to work, exceeding the threshold must serve as an advance warning rather than an indicator that the damage has already occurred. Option C is correct because if pitchers exhibit elevated torque over several pitches prior to tearing the ligament, the threshold provides actionable warning to remove the pitcher and prevent the injury. If, instead, the ligament tears on the very first pitch that exceeds the threshold, removing the pitcher afterward cannot prevent the tear. Option A is irrelevant because weather differences do not affect whether the sleeve's monitoring mechanism is effective at preventing tears. Option B is out of scope because throwing accuracy addresses game performance, not whether the sleeve prevents UCL tears. Option D is irrelevant because differences between starting and relief pitchers do not determine whether the threshold-based removal strategy works. Option E is out of scope because post-injury treatment outcomes have no bearing on the sleeve's ability to prevent the injury.

question: To reduce operating expenses, Zenith Bank replaced most of its human loan officers with an automated algorithm that evaluates and approves small-business loan applications. Over the following year, the average time required to process an application dropped from five days to two hours, and the default rate on loans approved by the algorithm was no higher than the historical default rate for loans approved by human officers. Bank executives concluded that switching to the automated system improved the overall profitability of Zenith’s small-business lending division. Which of the following is an assumption on which the bank executives’ conclusion depends?
option_a: The majority of small-business owners who applied for loans after the system was introduced were aware that their applications were being evaluated by an algorithm.
option_b: The algorithm’s criteria for evaluating loan applications did not rely on financial data that human loan officers were legally prohibited from considering.
option_c: The automated system did not achieve its acceptable default rate primarily by rejecting a large proportion of creditworthy applicants who would have been approved by human loan officers.
option_d: Other commercial banks that introduced automated lending systems did not experience an increase in operational errors.
option_e: The human loan officers who were replaced were not reassigned to other departments within Zenith Bank where their compensation continued to be an expense for the bank.
explanation: The correct answer is C. The executives conclude that overall profitability improved based on two operational metrics: faster processing times and a default rate no higher than before. However, profitability depends on net revenue, which is a function of the total volume of performing, interest-generating loans issued minus operating costs and defaults. If the algorithm kept default rates low simply by being excessively conservative and turning away many creditworthy borrowers who would have generated substantial profit, overall division profits could easily have fallen. Therefore, the argument depends on the assumption that the system did not eliminate a large volume of profitable loans in this manner. Option A is incorrect because customer awareness of the evaluation method is irrelevant to the division's financial bottom line. Option B is incorrect because regulatory compliance, while important legally, does not directly impact the mathematical validity of the profitability conclusion. Option D is incorrect because the outcomes at other banks do not bear on Zenith's internal division results. Option E is incorrect because the conclusion specifically concerns the profitability of Zenith's small-business lending division; even if former officers were reassigned elsewhere, their salaries would no longer be expenses incurred by this specific division.

question: Over the past decade, several professional baseball teams have utilized high-speed motion-tracking systems to analyze pitchers' throwing mechanics. Coaches found that pitchers who adjusted their delivery to maximize the rotational spin of the ball significantly reduced the number of hits they conceded per game. Citing these results, a coalition of youth sports coaches has recommended that amateur baseball academies implement similar tracking technology, arguing that teaching these optimized mechanics to adolescent pitchers will improve their competitive performance while lowering their risk of throwing-related arm injuries. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the coalition’s recommendation?
option_a: The mechanical adjustments required to maximize rotational spin subject developing joints and ligaments to significantly greater structural stress than conventional throwing motions do.
option_b: The high-speed optical tracking systems currently used by professional teams are difficult to calibrate properly without specialized technicians.
option_c: Adolescent pitchers who throw with high pitch velocity do not necessarily concede fewer hits than those who rely primarily on pitch location and timing.
option_d: Most amateur baseball academies prioritize overall athletic development over preparing their athletes for professional sports careers.
option_e: Many professional pitchers who adopted the optimized mechanics had already suffered minor arm injuries earlier in their careers.
explanation: The coaches' recommendation depends on the claim that training adolescent pitchers to maximize ball spin will both improve performance and reduce the risk of throwing-related arm injuries. The statement pointing out that the mechanical adjustments required to maximize rotational spin place significantly greater structural stress on developing joints and ligaments directly weakens the argument by showing that adopting these mechanics is likely to increase, rather than decrease, injury risk in young players. The statement regarding the technical difficulty of calibrating professional tracking systems raises a practical hurdle to implementation but does not undermine the merits of the mechanics themselves. The statement comparing pitch velocity to pitch location and timing is irrelevant because the stimulus specifically focuses on pitch spin, not velocity. The statement concerning the broader priorities of amateur academies does not address whether the recommended mechanics actually achieve the stated performance and safety outcomes. Finally, the statement noting that professional pitchers had previously suffered arm injuries merely describes past medical history and provides no evidence that the new mechanics are harmful or ineffective for adolescents.

question: Researchers recently evaluated an interactive software application designed to deliver cognitive behavioral therapy to individuals suffering from chronic insomnia. In controlled clinical trials, patients who completed the application's full eight-week regimen showed improvements in sleep duration and quality comparable to those achieved by patients receiving in-person treatment from licensed sleep specialists. However, when a health network made the application freely accessible to all of its insomnia patients, the proportion of patients who experienced meaningful sleep improvement was dramatically lower than the proportion typically achieved through in-person specialist care, even though both groups presented with similar initial symptom severity. Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described above?
option_a: Chronic insomnia is generally more resistant to cognitive behavioral therapy when it is accompanied by severe physical pain rather than psychological distress.
option_b: Patients receiving in-person treatment from sleep specialists were considerably more likely to report satisfaction with their overall care than were patients who used the software application.
option_c: The software application was periodically updated during the rollout to include interactive relaxation modules that were not present in the version used during the clinical trials.
option_d: Many licensed sleep specialists advise their patients to maintain consistent waking times even on weekends.
option_e: Unlike patients treated in person by specialists, the vast majority of the health network's patients who began using the application ceased using it within the first three weeks.
explanation: The apparent discrepancy is that the software matched the effectiveness of in-person therapy in trials, yet resulted in substantially lower improvement rates when rolled out to the broader patient population. The correct option resolves this by pointing out that the clinical trial results applied specifically to patients who completed the full eight-week regimen; in the real-world rollout, most software users abandoned the application after only two or three weeks, failing to receive the therapeutic dose necessary to achieve the reported benefits. The option concerning patient satisfaction is irrelevant because subjective satisfaction with care does not explain why actual clinical sleep improvement was lower. The option noting the addition of relaxation modules fails to explain the discrepancy, as adding features provides no reason for treatment efficacy to plunge. The option regarding specialists advising regular wake times merely describes standard sleep advice that would be part of cognitive behavioral therapy generally and does not address the divergence in outcomes. Finally, the option regarding insomnia linked to physical pain is out of scope because the stimulus specifies that the patient groups had comparable initial symptom severity, and there is no reason to assume the rollout group suffered disproportionately from pain-related insomnia.

question: Psychologists conducted an experiment to test whether sleep enhances memory consolidation. Participants were instructed to memorize a list of unfamiliar vocabulary words. Immediately afterward, half of the participants took a 60-minute nap, while the other half remained awake and listened to an audiobook. When tested six hours later, the participants who had napped recalled substantially more of the vocabulary words than did those who had stayed awake. The psychologists concluded that sleep actively promotes the neurological consolidation of newly learned information. Which of the following is an assumption on which the psychologists' argument depends?
option_a: Listening to an audiobook does not require more cognitive effort than memorizing unfamiliar vocabulary words.
option_b: The difference in recall between the two groups was not primarily the result of the audiobook interfering with the retention of the vocabulary words.
option_c: People who regularly take afternoon naps do not have superior overall memory compared to those who do not.
option_d: The neurological processes that consolidate memories cannot occur while an individual is fully awake.
option_e: The participants who took the nap were able to fall asleep almost immediately after the memorization phase.
explanation: The correct option is the one stating that the difference in recall between the two groups was not primarily the result of the audiobook interfering with the retention of the vocabulary words. The argument attributes the napping group's superior performance specifically to the positive effect of sleep on consolidation. If listening to an audiobook caused retroactive interference (that is, competing verbal input actively impaired the waking group's memory), then the waking group performed worse because of the interference rather than because sleep enhanced consolidation in the napping group. Negating this statement directly undermines the conclusion. The option concerning cognitive effort is irrelevant because the relative effort of listening to an audiobook versus memorizing words does not affect whether the difference was caused by sleep consolidation. The option regarding the memory of people who regularly take afternoon naps is out of scope because the experiment tested the immediate effect of an intervention rather than long-term lifestyle habits. The option stating that memory consolidation cannot occur while awake is too extreme; the psychologists only argue that sleep actively promotes consolidation, not that it is the exclusive state in which consolidation happens. The option about falling asleep almost immediately is unnecessary, as the therapeutic effect of sleep on memory could still occur even if participants took some time to drift off.

question: In clinical trials for a newly developed prescription sleep medication, Drug X, participants fell asleep significantly faster and woke up less frequently during the night than did participants who received a placebo. Objective brain-wave monitoring confirmed that Drug X recipients slept an average of 45 minutes longer per night than the placebo group. Curiously, however, when evaluated the following afternoon, participants who took Drug X reported feeling noticeably more fatigued and scored significantly worse on cognitive reaction-time tests than those in the placebo group, even though Drug X is completely metabolized and eliminated from the body within four hours of ingestion. Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox described above?
option_a: Participants in the placebo group generally reported greater baseline optimism about the treatment than did participants in the Drug X group.
option_b: Participants who recorded the longest total sleep durations during the study also reported the highest levels of satisfaction with their sleep upon waking in the morning.
option_c: The cognitive reaction-time tests were administered to both groups under identical lighting and noise conditions in the laboratory.
option_d: Although Drug X lengthens total sleep time, it suppresses deep slow-wave sleep, the specific sleep stage most critical for cognitive restoration and daytime alertness.
option_e: A small proportion of participants in both the Drug X group and the placebo group reported mild physical side effects such as dry mouth during the first week of the study.
explanation: The paradox is that subjects taking Drug X slept objectively longer and experienced no lingering chemical presence of the drug the next day (due to its rapid four-hour clearance), yet they suffered from greater next-afternoon fatigue and impaired cognitive performance compared to those on a placebo. The statement noting that Drug X suppresses deep slow-wave sleep resolves the discrepancy by demonstrating that the quality of sleep was compromised; even though total sleep duration increased, the reduction of the specific sleep phase essential for mental restoration directly accounts for the next-day fatigue and poor cognitive scores. The statement regarding baseline optimism fails to explain the objective degradation in reaction-time scores, as subjective expectations do not account for measurable physiological deficits, especially in a controlled trial. The statement pointing out that longer-sleeping participants reported high satisfaction upon waking only deepens or runs parallel to the mystery, failing to explain why their afternoon performance deteriorated. The statement concerning identical testing conditions merely confirms that external environmental variables were controlled, offering no explanation for the divergence in results between the two groups. Finally, the statement regarding mild side effects affecting a small proportion of both groups is irrelevant, as it applies equally to both cohorts and does not account for the marked difference in afternoon fatigue.

question: Management of the Metros, a professional basketball team, recently analyzed game outcomes across several seasons to evaluate the impact of resting star players during grueling road trips. The analysis revealed that the Metros' winning percentage in away games in which star players were rested was virtually identical to their winning percentage in away games in which all star players played. Management concluded from this finding that the physical presence of star players on the court does not meaningfully enhance the team's probability of winning road games. Which of the following is an assumption on which management's conclusion depends?
option_a: Star players on other teams in the league were rested at roughly the same rate as star players on the Metros.
option_b: The Metros' offensive scoring average was not significantly lower in games played without star players than in games played with them.
option_c: The Metros won a higher percentage of their home games than of their away games over the seasons analyzed.
option_d: Ticket-holding fans at away venues were generally unaware in advance that star players would be rested.
option_e: The team did not disproportionately rest its star players in away games against opponents that were significantly weaker than average.
explanation: The argument concludes that star players do not improve the team's odds of winning away games because the team's winning percentage was the same with or without them. This reasoning assumes that the two sets of games are comparable in terms of difficulty. If the team predominantly rested its stars against weak opponents—whom they could beat even with a depleted roster—and played them against top-tier opponents, the win rate without stars would be artificially inflated by easier matchups. Thus, assuming the team did not disproportionately rest stars against weaker opponents is required for the conclusion to hold. The resting habits of opposing teams are irrelevant to assessing the internal performance of the Metros. The claim regarding the offensive scoring average is unnecessary because the argument is strictly about winning games, not offensive efficiency or points scored. Comparing home game records to away game records is irrelevant because the argument pertains solely to away game outcomes. Finally, whether attending fans knew in advance that stars would sit out has no bearing on game outcomes or the athletic impact of the players.

question: Several large corporate accounting firms recently adopted artificial intelligence software to automate the auditing of client financial records. The software performs routine data verification and error detection far faster and more accurately than entry-level auditors. Firm executives expected that deploying this software would reduce the overall hours senior auditors needed to spend on each engagement and decrease the total number of errors that went undetected. However, over the two years following widespread adoption of the software, senior auditors at these firms reported spending substantially more hours per audit, and the number of major financial misstatements discovered only after audits were completed actually increased. Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy described above?
option_a: Most clients of the accounting firms had not upgraded their own computer networks to make them fully compatible with the new auditing software.
option_b: The licensing fees and maintenance costs associated with the artificial intelligence software exceeded the financial savings gained from hiring fewer entry-level auditors.
option_c: Senior auditors with decades of experience were initially far more skeptical of the software's accuracy than were less experienced staff members.
option_d: The routine manual reviews previously conducted by entry-level auditors had inadvertently caught subtle, contextual irregularities that the software was not designed to detect, which senior auditors had to spend long hours diagnosing whenever financial summaries failed to reconcile.
option_e: Entry-level auditors who were trained primarily on artificial intelligence software were less likely to stay with their firms for more than two years than entry-level auditors had been in the past.
explanation: The paradox centers on why replacing human entry-level auditors with faster, more accurate software caused senior auditors to work more hours and led to more undetected errors surfacing after audits were finalized. The finding that manual reviews by entry-level auditors previously caught subtle, contextual anomalies outside the software's programming resolves both parts of the paradox: senior auditors had to expend substantial extra time troubleshooting when summary numbers failed to reconcile due to these unflagged anomalies, and because the software missed these non-standard errors entirely, more of them went unnoticed through the end of the audit.
